Some systems switch in milliseconds (unnoticed by electronics); others take seconds, briefly resetting clocks and computers.
Solar panels alone don't keep the lights on in a blackout.

cards.title: Charges essentielles
cards.text: Plutôt que de sécuriser toute la maison, de nombreux systèmes alimentent un tableau de « charges essentielles » : réfrigérateur, éclairage, box, commande de la chaudière, quelques prises.

deep.x: Backing up a whole house needs large batteries and inverters. Many systems instead back up a selected "essential loads" circuit.
Typical consumption
How long

x: 10 kWh battery, 400 W average essential load

deep.x: Avoid on backup
Ovens, water heaters, EV chargers and heaters drain batteries quickly and are usually excluded.
Back up what matters, not everything.

cards.title: Onduleur de secours pour l'électronique

steps: La batterie de l'onduleur prend le relais en millisecondes

cards.text: Une alimentation sans interruption (onduleur) maintient un ordinateur, un NAS ou le réseau en marche pendant quelques minutes lors d'une coupure et permet un arrêt propre. Elle est caractérisée en VA et en autonomie à une charge donnée.

deep.x: An uninterruptible power supply (UPS) keeps computers and network equipment running through short outages and protects against power disturbances.

steps: Clean shutdown or bridge to restoration

deep.x: Types

items.b: switches to battery when needed, cheap

deep.x: Sizing
Uses
A UPS buys time to save work and shut down safely.

cards.title: Groupes électrogènes

items.r: inverseur posé par un électricien
le faire tourner dehors, loin des fenêtres

cards.text: Les groupes électrogènes portables à essence assurent un secours, mais ne doivent jamais fonctionner à l'intérieur (monoxyde de carbone). Le raccorder à la maison exige un inverseur de source adapté, pour qu'il ne puisse pas alimenter le réseau.

deep.x: Portable generators provide backup power for long outages, but they must be used safely.

items.w: Running a generator in the garage or indoors
items.r: Always outdoors, far from windows and doors

deep.x: Carbon monoxide
Engines produce carbon monoxide, an invisible, odourless gas that can kill within minutes in enclosed spaces. Use CO alarms.
Connecting to the house
Back-feeding through a socket can electrocute line workers and damage the generator.
Sizing
Generators belong outside, connected through a proper switch.

cards.title: Du véhicule à la maison
cards.text: Certains VE peuvent alimenter une maison grâce à la recharge bidirectionnelle (V2H) ou alimenter des appareils via une prise (V2L). Une batterie de VE de 70 kWh pourrait alimenter un logement type pendant des jours.

deep.x: Electric car batteries are large energy stores. Bidirectional charging lets some EVs power appliances or even a whole home.

items.b: vehicle-to-load: sockets on the car power appliances
vehicle-to-home: car powers house through a bidirectional charger

deep.x: Scale
Requirements
Examples
Several models offer V2L sockets (such as some Hyundai, Kia and MG cars), while V2H requires compatible cars and chargers, still relatively rare in Europe.
Your car's battery could keep the house running for days.

cards.title: Rentabilité

items: Gros écart de prix entre heures pleines et creuses

cards.text: Les batteries domestiques ne se rentabilisent pas toujours par les seules économies. Le dossier s'améliore avec une forte consommation du soir, des tarifs horaires, de faibles prix de rachat, ou un fort besoin de secours.

deep.x: Home batteries don't always pay for themselves through savings alone. The business case depends on how they're used.
A simple estimate

x: 7 kWh battery cycling 300 days a year

deep.x: With a battery costing several thousand euros, simple payback can exceed ten years.
What improves the case
Batteries often make more sense for resilience than for pure savings.

cards.title: Sécurité et emplacement
cards.text: Installez les batteries dans un endroit ventilé, frais et sec, à l'écart des chambres et des issues, avec les dégagements indiqués par le fabricant. La chimie LFP est préférée pour les logements car elle est plus stable thermiquement.

deep.x: Home batteries store a lot of energy. Proper placement and installation reduce fire risk and extend battery life.
Chemistry choice
Temperature
Certification
Choose batteries certified to recognised safety standards and installed by qualified installers, with proper protection and isolation.
A well-placed LFP battery is a safe neighbour.

Parce que le soleil se couche

quiz.q: Comment dimensionner une batterie domestique ?
options: Égale à la taille des panneaux
Autour de votre consommation du soir et de la nuit
quiz.explain: Stockez ce que vous achèteriez sinon après le coucher du soleil.

quiz.explain: Le monoxyde de carbone est mortel.

lessons.title: Une histoire de l'électricité
lessons.summary: De l'ambre au réseau intelligent.

cards.title: L'ambre et le mot « électrique »
cards.text: Les Grecs de l'Antiquité avaient remarqué que l'ambre frotté attirait les plumes. Le mot grec pour l'ambre, « elektron », nous a donné « électricité », un terme forgé par William Gilbert vers 1600.

deep.x: Electricity's name comes from amber. Ancient Greeks noticed that rubbed amber attracted light objects like feathers and straw.
Gilbert's work
English physician William Gilbert's 1600 book "De Magnete" studied magnetism and static electricity, coining the Latin word "electricus" (amber-like) for materials that attract when rubbed.
Elektron

items.b: first used in English by Thomas Browne, 1646

deep.x: Early experiments
Electricity is named after a fossilised tree resin.

cards.title: La pile de Volta, 1800
cards.text: Alessandro Volta a empilé des disques de zinc et de cuivre séparés par du tissu imbibé de saumure : la première pile à donner un courant régulier. Le volt porte son nom.

deep.x: Alessandro Volta's "voltaic pile" was the first source of steady electric current, opening the door to modern electrical science.
The frog debate
Luigi Galvani had observed frog legs twitching with metals and believed in "animal electricity". Volta argued the metals generated the electricity and built the pile to prove it.
Consequences
Humphry Davy used powerful batteries to isolate sodium and potassium in 1807.
Honour
The volt is named after Volta. Napoleon made him a count in recognition of his work.
The battery turned electricity from sparks into a steady flow.

cards.title: Les découvertes de Faraday

items.l: découverte à la base de tous les générateurs

cards.text: En 1831, Michael Faraday a montré que des aimants en mouvement induisent des courants, principe de tout générateur et de tout transformateur. Il avait peu d'instruction formelle et est devenu l'un des plus grands expérimentateurs de tous les temps.

deep.x: Michael Faraday, largely self-taught, made some of the most important discoveries in electrical science.

items.l: born to a blacksmith's family in London

deep.x: From apprentice to scientist
Faraday left school early and became a bookbinder's apprentice, reading the books he bound. He attended Humphry Davy's lectures and became his assistant at the Royal Institution.
His legacy
The farad
The unit of capacitance, the farad, honours him.
Faraday started the Royal Institution's Christmas Lectures for young people in 1825; they continue today.

cards.title: Les équations de Maxwell
cards.text: Dans les années 1860, James Clerk Maxwell a écrit quatre équations unifiant électricité, magnétisme et lumière. Elles prédisaient les ondes radio, que Hertz a démontrées en 1887.

deep.x: In the 1860s, James Clerk Maxwell described electricity, magnetism and light in one theory. It remains one of the greatest achievements in physics.
The prediction
Maxwell's equations showed that changing electric and magnetic fields create waves travelling at the speed of light, so light itself must be an electromagnetic wave.
The four equations in words

items.b: magnetic field lines have no start or end
changing magnetic fields create electric fields
currents and changing electric fields create magnetic fields

deep.x: Impact
Maxwell revealed that light is electricity and magnetism dancing together.

cards.title: Ampoules électriques

events.l: Centrale de Pearl Street, New York

cards.text: De nombreux inventeurs ont travaillé sur l'éclairage électrique. En 1879, Edison et, en Grande-Bretagne, Swan ont produit des ampoules à filament de carbone pratiques et durables. Edison a aussi construit les centrales et le réseau pour vendre l'électricité.

deep.x: Electric light transformed daily life. Many inventors contributed, but Edison and Swan produced the first practical long-lasting bulbs around 1879.
Edison's system
Edison's genius was not only the bulb but the whole system: generators, wiring, meters and fuses. His Pearl Street station in New York opened in 1882.
Ediswan
After a patent dispute in Britain, Edison and Swan merged their British companies in 1883 as "Ediswan".
From filaments to LEDs
Nobel Prize
Isamu Akasaki, Hiroshi Amano and Shuji Nakamura received the 2014 Nobel Prize in Physics for blue LEDs, which made white LED lighting possible.
The light bulb needed a whole electrical system to shine.

cards.title: L'électricité au Portugal
cards.text: Les premières lumières électriques du Portugal ont été allumées à Cascais en 1878. De grands barrages hydroélectriques à partir des années 1950, sur des fleuves comme le Zêzere et le Douro, ont porté l'électrification du pays.

deep.x: Electricity reached Portugal in the late 19th century, and hydropower drove electrification across the 20th century.

events.l: Central Tejo power station in Lisbon

deep.x: Central Tejo
Lisbon's Central Tejo power station, built in stages from 1909, supplied much of the city's electricity until the 1970s. It's now part of the MAAT museum in Belém.
Hydro era

items: Castelo do Bode on the Zêzere

deep.x: No nuclear
Portugal never built a nuclear power plant. A project at Ferrel, near Peniche, was abandoned in the 1970s after local protests.
Modern era
Portugal electrified with water, then wind and sun.

cards.title: Le transistor, 1947
cards.text: Aux laboratoires Bell, Bardeen, Brattain et Shockley ont construit le premier transistor. Il a remplacé les encombrants tubes à vide et rendu possibles l'électronique moderne, les ordinateurs et les téléphones.

deep.x: The transistor, invented at Bell Labs in December 1947, is the foundation of all modern electronics.
The inventors
John Bardeen, Walter Brattain and William Shockley shared the 1956 Nobel Prize in Physics for the transistor.
Scale
What a transistor does

items.b: small signal controls a larger one

deep.x: Billions of tiny switches now fit on a fingernail-sized chip.

cards.title: Nucléaire et renouvelables

events.l: coût du solaire en baisse de ~90 %

cards.text: Les premières centrales nucléaires sont apparues dans les années 1950. À partir des années 2000, l'éolien puis le solaire se sont développés rapidement à mesure que les coûts baissaient ; le prix des modules solaires a chuté d'environ 90 % dans les années 2010.

deep.x: The second half of the 20th century brought nuclear power; the 21st brought the rapid rise of wind and solar.
Falling costs
Nuclear today
Nuclear provides around a tenth of the world's electricity, with low carbon emissions but high construction costs and long build times.
Renewables today
Wind and solar are now the cheapest sources of new electricity in many countries, and their share grows every year.
Renewables went from expensive niche to cheapest option in about a decade.

cards.title: Des unités qui portent des noms de personnes
cards.text: De nombreuses unités honorent des scientifiques : volt (Volta), ampère (Ampère), ohm (Ohm), watt (Watt), hertz (Hertz), coulomb (Coulomb), tesla (Tesla).

deep.x: Most electrical units honour scientists who made key discoveries.
More units
Writing rules

items.r: 230 volts (230 V), 10 amps (10 A)

deep.x: Unit names are lowercase when written out; symbols for units named after people are capitalised.
James Watt worked on steam engines, not electricity, but his name became the universal unit of power.

cards.title: Et ensuite ?
cards.text: L'électricité prend en charge une part croissante de l'énergie utilisée : voitures, chauffage, industrie. Les défis sont désormais le stockage, l'extension du réseau et l'ajustement d'une offre renouvelable variable à la demande.

deep.x: Electricity is taking over more of the energy system. The challenges now are storage, grids and flexibility.
Electrification

items.l: electricity's share of global final energy
as cars, heating and industry electrify

deep.x: Challenges
Data centres and AI
Rapid growth of data centres, driven partly by AI, is increasing electricity demand in several countries, including new projects in Portugal such as at Sines.
The future of energy is increasingly electric.
